findings.reason: the followup is the plan's own dispatch route, so a new section it omits is a node no one dispatches, and §7 (unlike §2-§6) declares no section-level relation to place it either.
findings.text: the driving followup f-tprt-002 carries the dispatch order "§2, §3, §4, §5 in turn (each writes reckon/doccheck.py); §6 once its three gates open" and was not updated when §7 was added, so the route a coordinator dispatches from names every section except §7 and never reaches it

findings.reason: a change confined to roadmap.py leaves the same gate a plan-level blocker in the page a reader actually opens, which is the misreport the section exists to remove; the plan must either add serve.py and mcp_views.py to its write paths or move the scoping into the shared helper every caller already imports.
findings.text: §7 says "the change is confined to the readiness pass and the row it emits" and lists `reckon/roadmap.py` alone as its write path, but the misreport it fixes is computed by three call sites of the same helper: `reckon/roadmap.py:3104/3199`, `reckon/serve.py:2261` (into `plan["effective_status"]` at 2264, which the served plan page and fleet index read) and `reckon/mcp_views.py:2470` (into `effective_status` at 2544), so the served page and the MCP view would still report this plan blocked by a gate on one later section

findings.reason: the measure tests an internal readiness flag while the cited comment (c-gate-blocks-plan-1010) names `effective_status: blocked`, so the gate can go green on precisely the code path that leaves the reported defect live; the done-when must assert the reported status, or the deliverable must name the separate field the held section's gate is reported under.
findings.text: §7's done-when asserts only that plan `p` appears in `ready_now` with the gate reported against `s2`, never that the plan's reported status has cleared, while the deliverable simultaneously requires "the gate is still reported on the plan's row" (`row["gate_blockers"]`, roadmap.py:3222) — the very list `effective_status()` consumes at roadmap.py:3199, so a node that keeps the gate on the row passes this gate with `effective_status` still `blocked`
